config.title: Sudoku Solver

intro.title: Sudoku Solver
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Sudoku solver program that can automatically fill in a 9x9 puzzle grid while following the rules of Sudoku. You will learn the core concept of backtracking, a recursive algorithm that tries possible numbers in empty cells and undoes choices that lead to dead ends. The implementation will use fundamental JavaScript constructs like arrays, loops, conditionals, and functions. By the end, you'll understand how to apply algorithmic thinking to solve constraint-based lessons step by step.
intro.usecase: Sudoku solvers demonstrate constraint satisfaction lessons, a pattern used in real-world scheduling and resource allocation systems. For example, airline crew scheduling dashboards use similar backtracking algorithms to assign flights while respecting legal limits and availability. Calendar optimization tools in productivity apps apply these techniques to find meeting times that satisfy all participants' constraints. Even game development uses these algorithms for procedural level generation in puzzle games, ensuring solvable layouts.

objectives: Implement a function to validate Sudoku board entries against row, column, and subgrid constraints
Construct a recursive backtracking algorithm to solve a Sudoku puzzle
Manipulate a 2D array data structure to represent and update the Sudoku board state
Initialize a Sudoku solver with a starting board configuration
Apply constraint checking at each step of the solving process to prune invalid moves
Configure the solver to return the completed board or indicate unsolvable puzzles
